title: Replacing and Scanning Text
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of replacing and scanning text in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply replacing and scanning text in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to processing text in batches and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Replacing and Scanning Text through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding replacing and scanning text helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Replacing and Scanning Text helps you reason about sub and gsub. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: sub and gsub. Then connect it to scan. The remaining syllabus points—Extracting repeated matches, Processing text in batches—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports replacing and scanning text. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for replacing and scanning text using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Processing text in batches), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Run, troubleshoot, and reset
content_blocks.text: Save as lesson.rb and run `ruby lesson.rb` from a terminal. CodeLeaf currently has no isolated Ruby runner, so these examples should be run locally until one is deployed. If the command fails, confirm `ruby --version`, inspect the full error message, and verify that required standard-library or gem dependencies are installed. Reset by removing temporary files created by your experiment and returning the code to the smallest reproducible example.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain replacing and scanning text, identify its place in regular expressions, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
